questions.stem: The formula of the coordination compound which shows both coordination isomerism and linkage isomerism is:
questions.solution: Coordination isomerism requires both cationic and anionic complex species (present in A, C, D). Linkage isomerism requires an ambidentate ligand. In option C, $\mathrm{SCN^-}$ is an ambidentate ligand (can coordinate via S or N). Thus, C shows both types of isomerism.

questions.stem: The number of stereoisomers possible for the octahedral complex $[\text{Co}(\text{ox})_2(\text{Br})_2]^{3-}$ (where $\text{ox}$ is oxalate) is ________.
questions.solution:
The complex is of the type $[M(AA)_2B_2]$ where $AA$ is a symmetrical bidentate ligand.
This complex exhibits two geometrical isomers: cis and trans.
The trans-isomer is symmetrical (has plane of symmetry) and is optically inactive (1 form).
The cis-isomer is unsymmetrical (lacks plane of symmetry) and exists as a pair of enantiomers (dextro and laevo forms).
Total number of stereoisomers = 1 (trans) + 2 (cis-d & cis-l) = 3.

questions.stem: The complex showing optical activity is:
questions.solution: $\text{cis-}[\mathrm{Co(en)_2Cl_2}]^+$ lacks a plane of symmetry (and centre of symmetry) and is therefore chiral and optically active. Its trans isomer has a plane of symmetry and is optically inactive.

questions.stem: The total number of possible stereoisomers for the complex $[\text{Co}(\text{en})_2\text{Cl}_2]^+$ is _______.
questions.solution:
$[\text{Co}(\text{en})_2\text{Cl}_2]^+$ exists as cis and trans isomers.
Trans-isomer is optically inactive (meso-like/symmetrical).
Cis-isomer exists as a pair of enantiomers ($d$ and $l$ form).
Total number of stereoisomers $= 1 \text{ (trans)} + 2 \text{ (cis- }d/l\text{)} = 3$.

questions.stem: The number of geometrical isomers possible for the complex $[\mathrm{Pt(NH_3)(NH_2OH)(Py)(NO_2)}]^{+}$ is:
questions.solution: The complex is of the type $[\mathrm{Mabcd}]$, where $\mathrm{M}$ is a square planar metal center. For a square planar complex of the type $[\mathrm{Mabcd}]$, three geometrical isomers are possible by keeping one ligand fixed and varying the position of the other three.

questions.stem: The sum of the number of geometrical isomers of $[\mathrm{Co(en)_2Cl_2}]^+$ and $[\mathrm{Cr(ox)_2Cl_2}]^{3-}$ is ____________.
questions.solution:
$[\mathrm{Co(en)_2Cl_2}]^+$ is an $\mathrm{M(AA)_2B_2}$ type complex which has 2 geometrical isomers (cis and trans).
$[\mathrm{Cr(ox)_2Cl_2}]^{3-}$ is also of the form $\mathrm{M(AA)_2B_2}$ type, having 2 geometrical isomers (cis and trans).
Sum of geometrical isomers $= 2 + 2 = 4$.

questions.stem: The number of geometrical isomers possible for the complex $\left[\mathrm{Pt}(\mathrm{NH}_3)(\mathrm{NH}_2\mathrm{OH})(\mathrm{py})(\mathrm{NO}_2)\right]^+$ is:
questions.solution: The complex is of the square planar type $[\mathrm{Mabcd}]$, where $a, b, c, d$ are four different monodentate ligands. A square planar complex of type $[\mathrm{Mabcd}]$ has $3$ geometrical isomers (by fixing one ligand and varying the trans position of the other three).

questions.stem: The total number of possible coordination isomers for the complex $[\mathrm{Co(NH_3)_6}][\mathrm{Cr(CN)_6}]$ is _________.
questions.solution:
The coordination isomers are generated by gradual exchange of ligands:
1) $[\mathrm{Co(NH_3)_6}][\mathrm{Cr(CN)_6}]$
2) $[\mathrm{Co(NH_3)_5(CN)}][\mathrm{Cr(NH_3)(CN)_5}]$
3) $[\mathrm{Co(NH_3)_4(CN)_2}][\mathrm{Cr(NH_3)_2(CN)_4}]$
4) $[\mathrm{Co(NH_3)_3(CN)_3}][\mathrm{Cr(NH_3)_3(CN)_3}]$
5) $[\mathrm{Co(NH_3)_2(CN)_4}][\mathrm{Cr(NH_3)_4(CN)_2}]$
6) $[\mathrm{Co(NH_3)(CN)_5}][\mathrm{Cr(NH_3)_5(CN)}]$
7) $[\mathrm{Co(CN)_6}][\mathrm{Cr(NH_3)_6}]$
Thus, there are exactly 6 coordination isomers excluding the neutral-neutral duplicate/unstable combination or total 6 possible isomers.
